text:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] Prod /v1/generate latency SLO breach (p95=510ms > 400ms). routing-policy 'latency-slo-fallback' triggered 3x in last 5m. Paging @Mia (oncall). Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/alerts/1845001234

Mia (oncall): ack — I’m on it, checking routing decisions and policy triggers now.

Rahul (Runtime): seeing repeated route flips us-east1 -> eu-west1 -> us-east1. Policy history shows it also switched model variant to `redwood-13b-int8-fallback`.

Tilly (SRE): note — each reroute causes KV cache misses + coldwarm. That warmup spikes tail latency. Flapping makes the problem worse.

Sam (ProdEng): any customer reports? Jen, CS?

Jen (CS): Acme support called; they reported intermittent 500s and large latency since ~09:12 UTC. They asked if we're investigating.

Rahul (Runtime): quick hypothesis: the policy is 1m-window p95-based with no cooldown/hysteresis. When it reroutes to the fallback variant (which goes through a slightly different quantization execution path), tail latency increases, which immediately triggers another reroute back. Feedback loop.

Mia (oncall): can we disable the fallback policy quickly and pin prod routes to a stable variant? Pinning should stop cache churn.

Alex (Platform): I can toggle policy state. Options: console or API. API call: ```
curl -X POST \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/policies/latency-slo-fallback/disable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
Or via Console > Policies > latency-slo-fallback > Disable.

Mia (oncall): do it. Also add a temporary override to exclude known enterprise customers from automatic reroutes.

Alex (Platform): performed disable at 09:18:12 UTC. Policy state now: disabled. Confirming no new routing events in last 30s.

Tilly (SRE): monitoring: p95 falling from 510ms -> 130ms over 2m. KV cache fill shows warmup completed. No new region switches observed.

Rahul (Runtime): pinning prod-generate -> `redwood-13b-fp16-stable` for 30m to stop churn. Command used: ```
./rcp pin-route --service=prod-generate --model=redwood-13b-fp16-stable --ttl=30m
```
Pin confirmed.

Sam (ProdEng): quick impact estimate: ~17% of requests during the 8m incident window hit >400ms. We'll need to surface this to affected customers.

Jen (CS): Acme and BetaCorp reported visible impact. Notices sent for those accounts; CS will send follow-ups once we have a root cause summary.

Mia (oncall): handoff — Rahul, you take lead for the next 30m to drive mitigation and postmortem. I’ll continue monitoring for another 10m then handback.

Rahul (Runtime): taking lead. Immediate next steps: 1) capture full policy trigger history and decision log; 2) add cooldown (10m) + change trigger to require p99 > threshold for variant fallback; 3) change fallback target to a variant that shares execution path (avoid cache/quantization mismatch).

Alex (Platform): created CR-4782 for policy config changes and rollout plan. Will stage change in canary region before prod.

Tilly (SRE): SRE action items: add an alert suppression/annotation during planned policy ops and enhanced tracing for routing decisions so we can correlate cache misses to route flips.

Rahul (Runtime): quick log excerpt around flips: ```
[09:16:05] route-eval: p95=512ms -> trigger fallback -> target=redwood-13b-int8-fallback
[09:16:06] deploy-router: route-change -> region=eu-west1 model=redwood-13b-int8-fallback
[09:16:55] telemetry: tail-latency spike -> 640ms, cache-miss=1.0
[09:16:56] route-eval: p95=620ms -> revert route -> target=redwood-13b-fp16-stable
```
This pattern repeated ~3x.

Mia (oncall): status? any new pages?

Alex (Platform): IncidentBot updated: policy disabled + route pinned. No new pages.

IncidentBot: Incident state -> Mitigated (policy disabled, route pinned). Duration: 18m. Cleared pages.

Mia (oncall): good job everyone. Next: postmortem and customer-facing summary. Assigning owners: Rahul (root cause & runtime fix), Alex (policy config rollout), Tilly (observability + alert tuning), Jen (customer comms).

Rahul (Runtime): will follow up with a short runbook patch (how to safely enable fallback with cooldown and execution-path checks).

Jen (CS): customers notified; no escalations so far.

Mia (oncall): closing handoff — Rahul, please coordinate the postmortem doc and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:

Rahul (Runtime): will do. Leaving monitoring on.
